## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

## **Markdown**

Markdown is a lightweight set of conventions for formatting plain text files.

### **Headings**

Headings and subheadings can be included in a file to organize the document. make sure to leave a space between the \# and heading.

\# 1st Level Header

\## 2nd Level Header

\### 3rd Level Header

## Including R code chunks

R code chunks in R are include by pressing "Option+ Command + i"

`{#This is the R code chunk where R codes is written.}`

### **Links and Images**

Hyperlinks and external images or GIFs can be included in Quarto documents as well.

### Hyperlinks

- \[linked phrase\](<http://example.com>+) "if i remove the + sign, the link name will be shown as below."

- [linked phrase](http://example.com)

### **Text Formatting**

Basic formatting of text, such as italicizing, bolding, superscripts, and subscripts can be implemented as well.

| Raw text input   | Rendered output |
|------------------|-----------------|
| \*italic\*       | *italic*        |
| \*\*bold\*\*     | **bold**        |
| \`code\`         | code            |
| superscript\^2\^ | superscript2    |
| subscript\~2\~   | subscript2      |

## **Code Chunks**

adding **code chunks** to the file, allows us to run R code inside our document:

There are several ways to insert a code chunk:

1.  The keyboard shortcut Cmd/Ctrl + Alt + I (recommended)

2.  The “Insert” button icon ![](data:image/png;base64,) in the editor toolbar (top right).

3.  By manually typing the chunk delimiters

Activity_5:

➡️ Add a new code chunk at the bottom of the Quarto document, naming the chunk uptown-chunk by including **#\| label: uptown-chunk** as the first line inside the code chunk.

Solution:

```{r}
#| label: uptown-chunk
#| warning: true
scores <- c(3,5,2,8)
mean(scores)
```

Activity_6:

➡️ In the code chunk, use the include_graphics() function from the knitr package to include the image at the following URL: <https://github.com/dilernia/STA418-518/blob/main/uptownFunk2.png?raw=true>. Note that the URL should be enclosed in quotes when calling the include_graphics() function.

solution:

```{r}
#| label: uptown-chunk
#| echo: false

knitr::include_graphics("https://github.com/dilernia/STA418-518/blob/main/uptownFunk2.png?raw=true")

```

**Why use `knitr::include_graphics()`?**

- **Consistency:** It handles pathing seamlessly across different output formats (like HTML, PDF, and Word).

- **Quarto Integration:** It allows you to use chunk options like `#| out.width: "80%"` or `#| fig.align: "center"` to control how the image looks in your final document.
